candidates.title: Teleoperated 'centaur' robots enter dangerous physical labor
candidates.shift: A startup unveils a teleoperated centaur-like robot meant to perform hazardous physical tasks in place of humans, blending human control with a non-humanoid robot body.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: could preview a transitional labor category between full automation and human workers — remote-piloted hybrid machines for hazardous construction/warehouse tasks. Strange hybrid form is itself the signal.
candidates.evidence: Satyress's Threehalves robot, teleoperated, designed to aid humans in dangerous jobs exposing them to injury or death.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of a shift from full robotic autonomy to hybrid teleoperated human-robot labor forms, driven by the gap between hazardous-task demand and AI reliability. If common, construction and warehouse sites could deploy remote-piloted 'centaur' units, requiring new labor and insurance categories.
candidates.author: Ellen Eberhardt

candidates.title: 14MB on-device AI shrinks the compute footprint for physical AI
candidates.shift: A tiny 14MB agentic LLM built to run locally on phones, wearables, smart home devices and robots, bypassing cloud dependency entirely.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: if in-store robots/sensors can run AI on-device instead of via data centers, this reframes the 'compute?' question for retail infrastructure — less utility/data-center dependence, more edge hardware planning.
candidates.evidence: Cactus Compute's Needle2, described as a 14MB agentic LLM for phones, wearables, smart home and robots.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of a shift from centralized, cloud-compute-heavy AI toward edge/local physical AI, driven by cost, latency and privacy pressures. If it scales, retail robots and sensors could run AI without heavy data-center reliance, changing utility and infrastructure planning for stores.

candidates.title: Informal-settlement community platform models bottom-up public space
candidates.shift: A community-built 'platform' structure in Dhaka's Korail informal settlement, co-created with youth and local leaders, converts scarce open space into shared civic/commercial infrastructure.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: peripheral geography (Bangladesh) setting a participatory, low-cost model for generating public/commercial space in dense informal contexts — could inform bottom-up retail/civic infill elsewhere.
candidates.evidence: Paraa's Machan project at Ershad Maidan, Korail, built with community collaborators as a shared platform structure.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from top-down urban design to community co-created public infrastructure in dense informal settlements, driven by lack of formal open space. If replicated, could inform low-cost placemaking models for underserved retail/community corridors globally.
candidates.author: Pratik Mour

candidates.title: Landscape infrastructure as urban-edge/ecological corridor
candidates.shift: A corridor project in Cali, Colombia treats the boundary between city and mountain as infrastructure, restoring ecological continuity between urban fabric and a national park.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: peripheral-geography example of treating the 'wildland edge' as a formal infrastructure category — could preview new zoning/insurance treatments for urban-wildland interface real estate.
candidates.evidence: Edward Conde Serna Arquitectos' Cali Foothills Integral Corridor connecting urban fabric, Cristo Rey Ecopark, and the Farallones de Cali.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from hard urban edges to designed ecological buffer corridors, driven by climate/ecological restoration goals. If adopted broadly, could reshape zoning at urban-wildland interfaces relevant to peripheral retail sites.
candidates.author: Valentina Díaz

candidates.title: Multigenerational household building answers land-scarcity demographic shift
candidates.shift: A single building in peri-urban Hanoi houses three households — parents and two sons' families — as farmland converts to housing plots.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: single instance, but reflects demographic/land-scarcity pressure pushing multigenerational co-living into one structure — could presage similar formats reshaping mixed-use/retail real estate in dense Asian peripheries.
candidates.evidence: 100 Windows House / Inrestudio, in a Hanoi suburb where former farmland is becoming a town, houses three households in one building.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from single-family plots to multigenerational multi-household buildings under land pressure, driven by urbanization converting farmland. If widespread, could push mixed-use ground-floor retail models to adapt to multi-household demand patterns.
candidates.author: Pratik Mour

candidates.title: Old residential streetscapes reframed as commercial corridors
candidates.shift: Renovation of ordinary old residential houses into a 'cultural streetscape' commercial facility in a South Korean neighborhood.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: single instance of adaptive reuse converting residential fabric into retail/cultural use — a reframing that could inform low-capex retail infill strategies in aging urban cores elsewhere.
candidates.evidence: Koma Commercial Facility / U.GA Architects renovates old Western-style houses on Haeridan-gil into a commercial streetscape.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from purpose-built retail boxes to adaptive reuse of residential structures for commerce, driven by demand for authentic streetscape experience. If it spreads, could change how retailers value old residential stock for store format.
candidates.author: Pratik Mour

candidates.title: State-scale megacity construction sets new real-estate value benchmark
candidates.shift: China is reportedly building what's described as the world's first $2 trillion megacity — a state-directed urban development at an unprecedented capital scale.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: non-Western geography setting a new precedent for state-financed megacity construction, potentially resetting global benchmarks for what 'scale' means in construction finance.
candidates.evidence: Reported plans for a $2 trillion state-directed megacity project in China, per r/urbanplanning discussion.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of a shift from incremental urban growth to state-directed trillion-dollar megacity construction, driven by centralized capital deployment. If realized, it resets global scale expectations for construction finance and could pressure Western real estate capital models.

candidates.title: 3D-printed earth construction quietly diffuses beyond pilot house
candidates.shift: Five years after the TECLA raw-earth 3D-printed house, the underlying technology reportedly continues developing and spreading across new contexts.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: diffusion of 3D-printed earth construction beyond a single showcase project could signal a maturing low-carbon, low-cost building method reaching commercial construction — worth watching for craft-labor implications.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily reports TECLA's 3D-earth-printing technology has 'quietly spread across several' contexts five years after its debut.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from novelty pilot to diffusing construction method using 3D-printed raw earth, driven by low-carbon material demand and cost pressure. If it scales, could give developers a rapid, low-carbon build option for stores in emerging markets.
candidates.author: Moises Carrasco
